definition: The proportion of customers who stopped using or subscribing within a set period and standard.

definition: The proportion of customers who stopped using or subscribing within a set period and standard.

definition: The proportion of existing customers classified as churned because they did not perform a standard activity such as repurchase within a set period. You first set the product purchase cycle and the customer group before calculating.
example: We define this analysis's churn rate as the proportion of existing buyers with no repurchase in the last 6 months.
note: The period is set according to the company's analysis purpose. It is a different metric from a web page's bounce rate or checkout-step drop-off.

definition: The camera's height and direction in viewing the subject.
example: Let me lower the angle.

definition: A shooting composition looking down from a position higher than the subject.
example: Let me shoot the table scene from a high angle.
note: We group the high angle together as a Korean shooting term. Distinguish it from the top shot, a directly overhead vertical composition.

definition: A shooting composition looking up from a position lower than the subject.
example: Please frame the person from a low angle.
note: Organized as the Korean shooting term corresponding to the low angle.

definition: A camera composition set at the subject's eye level.
example: We film interviews at eye level.

definition: A camera composition that tilts the horizon.
example: We express an uneasy mood with a Dutch angle.

definition: A shot shown as if it were the view a character sees.
example: We attach a POV after the scene of opening the door.

definition: A shot showing the other person over one character's shoulder.
example: We'll continue the conversation scene with OTS.

definition: A shot that frames a face or subject closely to show detail.
example: Please capture the expression in a close-up.

definition: A shot that shows a very small part such as an eye or a hand enlarged.
example: We film just the pupil in an extreme close-up.

definition: A shot that frames a person's upper body to show expression and surroundings together.
example: We'll go with a medium shot for the explanation scene.

definition: A shot that frames the whole person and surrounding space widely.
example: We need a long shot to show the space.

definition: A shot that captures a wide background and a small subject together from far away.
example: We open the city view with an extreme long shot.

definition: A shot looking straight down from directly above the subject.
example: We capture the cooking process with a top shot.

definition: A person composition framing roughly from above the chest to the head.
example: We'll go with a bust shot for the interview.
note: Shot boundaries vary by on-set convention. Agree specifically on where on the chest to frame.

definition: A person composition framing from around the waist to the head.
example: We capture the hand gestures with a waist shot.
note: WS is, in some documents, also the abbreviation for Wide Shot. Don't rely on the abbreviation alone; confirm the framing.

definition: A composition framing the whole person from head to toe.
example: Please include the shoes in the full shot.

definition: A composition framing from around the knees to the head.
example: We show the movement with a knee shot.

definition: A shot framed around a single person.
example: We also film each person's one shot.

definition: A shot framing two people together.
example: We start the conversation with a two shot.

definition: A shot framing several people in one frame.
example: The last one is a group shot.

definition: The basic unit of footage captured in a single composition.
example: We attach a reaction after this shot.
note: The same English word shot is written with several Korean spellings. We linked them to one entry rather than inflating the count with different word forms.

definition: A story unit that continues in roughly the same time and place.
example: This scene takes place in a cafe.

definition: A bundle of related scenes that together form a part of the story.
example: The chase sequence is done.
note: Here it means a story unit. In editing software it can also refer to a timeline working unit where multiple clips are arranged.

definition: A shot filmed in one long stretch without cutting midway.
example: We capture from the entrance in a long take.

definition: The empty space between the top of the head and the top of the frame.
example: Reduce the head room a little.

definition: The empty space placed in the direction of the subject's gaze.
example: Please give eye room on the right.

definition: The empty space in the direction a person or object is moving.
example: We leave lead room in front of the runner.

definition: A filming instruction to track a moving subject within the frame.
example: Follow the actor as they walk up.
note: It refers to the aim of tracking a subject. It can be done by panning in place or by moving the camera. It differs from the follow focus, a focus-control device.

definition: Each individual attempt at filming the same shot.
example: Let's check with the third take.

definition: Footage selected as usable.
example: This take is an OK cut.

definition: Footage kept as a candidate rather than discarded right away.
example: Let's keep this version too.

definition: A shot that separately emphasizes an important object or action in a scene.
example: We need an insert of the signing hand.

definition: Supplementary footage added to the main footage to show the situation and mood.
example: Please also shoot B-roll of the workshop.

definition: A term for finishing and wrapping up the work in hand.
example: Let's wrap today's shoot here.
note: A common expression for wrapping up work across many worksites. The example for the video entry is written to fit the shooting situation. It can be rephrased as 'end of shoot' or 'wrap-up'.

definition: An action of turning the camera's direction left and right while keeping its position.
example: Pan toward the entrance.

definition: An action of turning the camera's direction up and down while keeping its position.
example: Tilt up from the feet to the face.

definition: A pan fast enough to blur the frame as it turns left and right.
example: We reveal the next person with a whip pan.

definition: A move in which the camera itself gets closer to the subject.
example: We dolly in to match the expression.

definition: A move in which the camera itself moves away from the subject.
example: We dolly out so the space becomes visible.

definition: Increasing the focal length to make the subject appear larger in the frame.
example: Zoom in on the sign.

definition: Decreasing the focal length to fit a wider range into the frame.
example: Zoom out so the surroundings are visible.

definition: A technique that combines camera movement with a zoom in the opposite direction to change the sense of perspective.
example: We use a dolly zoom at the tense moment.

definition: A method of filming while supporting the camera with the hands or shoulder.
example: We'll go handheld for the moving scene.
note: Demochi is an on-set term found in 1985 language-refinement materials.

definition: A stabilizing device that controls rotation axes to reduce camera shake.
example: Balance the gimbal first.
